conventions.convention: Permutation parameters act on zero-based slots; on one-based tuple positions use π̂(k)=1+π(k−1), and Uπ sends the factor in position π̂⁻¹(k) to position k.
The one-body reduction has trace one; the expectation of a sum of N slot observables is N times its one-particle trace pairing. For N=1 the reduction equals the original preparation.
The full spatial spin multiplicity is (2s+1)^N, and identical-particle permutations simultaneously permute spatial blocks and internal spin factors.
The Fourier transform uses exp(−2πix·ξ); consequently −aΔ has symbol 4π²a|ξ|². The Coulomb supplier is instantiated with mathematical masses m/(4π²) to obtain the declared physical kinetic operator.
N is positive. A zero fermionic sector has no trace-one preparation, its partition trace is zero, and no canonical normalization, ground eigenvalue or logarithm of its partition trace is used.

Entropy and Helmholtz free energy are defined here only for finite-dimensional sectors. Zero entropy summands are omitted without evaluating log 0. S=kB s, β=1/(kB T), T>0, and kB=1.380649×10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ exactly.

A thermal mean requires a finite absolute first spectral moment. An unbounded trace-product identity additionally requires the literal everywhere-defined trace-class left product; first-moment existence alone does not supply that product.

Fixed-N partition traces and full-Fock grand-canonical products are distinct. Countable fixed-N modes may have real energies bounded below; the grand-canonical product criteria use positive unshifted energies and require μ<inf εj for bosons.
Non-interacting means W=0; equivalence with κ=0 applies only to the Coulomb branch. Coulomb couplings g and κ have units J m, whereas occupation readouts use dimensionless particle count.

load_bearing.statement: Declares the positive-N species sector, one-particle operator and pair interaction, and constructs its assigned sector energy through bounded spatial, Coulomb spatial or finite-mode realizations; non-interacting means W=0.

For a declared bounded-below self-adjoint Gibbs generator G and β=1/(kB T), assumes 0<Z=Tr exp(−βG)<∞ and adopts ρβ=Z⁻¹exp(−βG) as the Gibbs preparation. Thermal means are finite absolute-first-moment spectral integrals.
On a nonzero finite-dimensional declared sector, s(ρ)=−Σwi log wi over positive eigenvalues, S=kB s and F(ρ)=tr(ρH)−kB T s(ρ); Feq=−β⁻¹log Z.

Under Countable Choice, for a finite-dimensional one-particle Hilbert space, n≥1 and a density operator on either permutation sector, its normalized one-body partial trace γ satisfies tr(ρ̃Σ(O))=n tr(γO) for every bounded O; γ is slot independent and equals ρ when n=1.

Under Countable Choice, the N-fold tensor product of L²(R³;Cʳ) is unitarily identified with L²(R³ᴺ;Cʳᴺ), with the stated combined spatial/internal permutation action and exact finite-component H² sector restrictions.

Under Countable Choice, for N,M≥1, a>0 and real essentially bounded V on R³ᴺ, −aΔ+V is self-adjoint on exactly W²,²(R³ᴺ;Cᴹ), bounded below by −ess sup|V|, with equivalent graph/Sobolev norms, a smooth compactly supported core and the stated imaginary resolvent formula.

Under Countable Choice, for a supplied countably infinite mode basis, N≥1 and real energies εj≥b, the symmetric and antisymmetric occupation vectors are complete orthonormal bases, their diagonal sector energies are self-adjoint, and 0<ZNσ(β)<∞ iff Σj exp(−βεj)<∞.

In the declared non-interacting finite-mode model, sector configurations have energy Σj λj εj and partition trace Σλ exp(−βΣj λj εj). On nonzero sectors the fermionic ground energy is the sum of the N smallest mode energies and the bosonic ground energy is N times the smallest.
In the finite-sector class with the adopted canonical preparation, unitary evolution preserves entropy, leaves ρβ stationary, and ρ(0)≠ρβ implies ρ(t)≠ρβ for every real t.

concerns.concern: Definition (d) says the reduction 'does not determine the sector preparation ρ: many sector preparations have the same one-body reduction' without restricting N or the model. This is false for the admitted N=1 branch: (b) explicitly gives γρ=ρ, so the reduction determines every preparation uniquely. It also cannot be noninjective on a one-dimensional sector. The general possibility of nonunique reductions needs qualification.

Definition (a), reiterated in (d)(ii), says AC 'is assumed only in the Coulomb realization'. However (a) adopts P2, P4 and P5, whose opened formulations expressly assume AC, and (e) invokes the general observable spectral-PVM and evolution readings with that hypothesis. The local bounded spatial realization is correctly CC-only, but that does not remove the inherited AC premise of these physical interfaces. Distinguish the operator construction's choice cost from the adopted framework assumptions, or supply an explicitly restricted CC-only reading.

The first Remark says 'a continuum of radiation modes has divergent free partition function by the cited one-particle non-compactness argument'. No item or source locator identifies that argument, and the continuum one-particle space, measure and energy operator are not declared. The opened suppliers establish discrete countable-mode criteria, not this continuum assertion. Supply the exact noncompactness result and its hypotheses before making the additional claim.

The two Example model specifications declare the spaces, statistics, N and h but never explicitly set the pair interaction W=0. Verification [L1] then invokes the non-interacting diagonalization theorem. The title conveys the intended choice, but the adopted fixed-N definition otherwise includes independent interaction data; state W=0 in the declared models.

The Burmistrov–Lunkin sources.references locator attributes the entropy-conservation remark to 'Section 1.1.1 printed page 13'. In the retrieved January 10, 2023 text it occurs in §1.1.3, printed page 14, immediately before §1.1.4; §1.1.1 supplies the Liouville equation instead. The underlying conservation claim is supported, but its locator is inaccurate. Checked against [the primary notes](https://home.itp.ac.ru/~burmi/HSE/Lectures-StatPhys-temp.pdf).

seams_checked.note: Contextual reading-order edge: no controlled-approximation theorem is invoked in the assigned item arguments.
Compared sector definitions and occupation-basis/count statements with consumers; positive N, canonical slot translation and zero fermionic sectors are preserved.
Tensor, partial-trace and bounded cyclicity statements match their uses. One-body reduction remains finite-dimensional; spatial products use the supplied Euclidean unitary.

Finite Gibbs supplier is not credited with uniqueness; that equality case is proved locally. Coulomb normalization is explicitly corrected by parameter substitution, bounded external addition is local, and fixed-N traces are separated from full-Fock products.
Spaces, spin components and bounded baseline scope match, but the declared-model definition's 'AC only in Coulomb' accounting omits AC explicitly assumed by adopted P5.

Outcome-law and moment uses preserve domains and integrability; the declared-model definition nevertheless claims AC is confined to Coulomb while adopting the general P2 spectral reading that assumes AC.
Flow signs, density conjugation and stationarity uses match. The declared-model definition's exclusive Coulomb AC wording conflicts with the AC premise of adopted P4 and its general spectral flow.
Energy, action and coupling units match. Temperature and entropy units are explicitly introduced locally; parameter identifications retain P7 qualifications.
Density and pure-state vocabulary matches; zero sectors are treated as admitting no preparation, rather than importing a trace-one state on the zero space.
The diagonal-adjoint supplier is used only for supplied countable bases, real diagonal energies and the exact squared-weight domain.
Finite bounded observables and their means are used within the supplier's hypotheses; probabilities and computed means are not presented as observed data.
Bond coupling is an energy, tτ/ħ is dimensionless, β has inverse-energy units, and site occupation is dimensionless.
The two-fermion three-mode and two-boson two-mode bases, dimensions and total occupations agree with the supplied occupation model.
Dilute identities retain their Bose/Fermi domains, and product convergence examples retain positive energies and the bosonic chemical-potential condition.
Two-site spectral phases and density evolution match the autonomous flow; nonproduction of the canonical preparation is a conditional exact model claim, with no empirical thermalization conclusion.
